STEP 1 - Vessel type: flat plate, square (white, rounded-corner, flat centre, no inner wall).

STEP 2 - Vessel size:
a) Square plates are typically 20-30 cm; this one looks like a standard medium-large square dinner plate, so about 26 cm.
b) Reference: the pizza slice is a standard slice. Its tip-to-crust length is roughly 60-70% of the plate width, which puts the plate near 25-27 cm across. Width is about 26 cm.
Final width = 26 cm, area = 676 cm².

STEP 3 - Food items:
- Pizza slice (countable, one slice): count = 1 slice, 30 g for a standard slice... but this is a thick-crust, topped slice, so use the slice rule: about 1.5 cm thick. Estimate the slice footprint: a triangle roughly 13 cm long and 9 cm wide at the crust, so area ≈ 0.5 × 13 × 9 ≈ 58 cm², roughly 60-65 cm² including the rounded crust. Volume = 60 cm² × 1.5 cm ≈ 90 ml. Density for bread-based pizza is closer to 0.5 g/ml than pure bread (0.3) because of cheese and sauce, so about 45-50 g. Taking a typical topped slice weight of around 100 g as a check against the footprint: the footprint method gives about 50 g, and standard topped pizza slices weigh 80-110 g, so I take the middle value of about 90 g as the crust-plus-topping mass.
- Mozzarella: white melted cheese covers about 30% of the slice, roughly 20 cm² × 0.3 cm ≈ 6 ml × 1.0 = 6 g, included in the slice mass above, so I count it within the pizza entry.
- Bacon or ham bits: several small pieces, about 3-4 g in total, also included in the slice.
- Tomato sauce: thin smear, included.

Hidden food: no base layer beyond the crust.

STEP 4 - Total mass is a single slice on a large plate: about 90 g.

STEP 5 - kcal per 100 g: pizza with cheese and meat (cooked weight) is about 270 kcal per 100 g.

Total ≈ 90 g, about 243 kcal.
